title: skills.lock/1
description: The skills lockfile: what hmd installed or suggested, and WHY. One format, two scopes: <project>/.planning/skills.lock (this project triggered or needs the skill; meant to be committed) and $HEIMDALL_HOME/skills.lock (machine scope: the first-run rows, such as superpowers and the marketplace). bin/lib/skills_lock.py writes and verifies it (`record`, `read`, `verify`); test/skills-lock.test.sh pins this file to that code's enums, caps and patterns, so the two cannot drift apart. ROWS: one per id per file. In the canonical text they are sorted by id, one per line, with a fixed key order, so the same records always give the same bytes and a committed lock diffs cleanly. A row is append-only except its state: suggested, declined and failed move freely among themselves and into installed or adopted; installed never goes back to suggested, declined or failed; adopted can only become installed. WHY: why.evidence is the matched token or file path ONLY, at most 64 characters with control and format characters removed, and never prompt text: the project file is committed. The other free-text fields (ref, version, source, pin, rule, via, run) are printable ASCII, the same rule the install receipt (bin/lib/install-receipt.sh) applies, so a receipt line and its lock row agree. `manifest_sha256` is the sha256 of skills.manifest.json when the file was last written, or null when the manifest could not be read; `at` and why.run say when, and in which run, the row last changed. `content_hash` is a git commit id for a cloned skill and null for a plugin (the CLI exposes no hash). JSON Schema cannot express cross-field rules, so `x-invariants` lists the extra rules `verify` enforces.

x-invariants.rule: entry ids are unique within the file
an entry's `at` is a real UTC calendar time (no 30 February, no hour 25)
why.evidence is stored in its cleaned form: no control, format or separator characters and no leading or trailing space
